sectionToMerge.h2: Frequently Asked Questions About PSMA PET/CT: Imaging for Prostate Cancer
sectionToMerge.intro: PSMA PET/CT is a specialised imaging scan that helps locate prostate cancer with high accuracy. These answers explain how the scan works, who it may suit, what it costs, and how international patients can access it.

items.q: What is a PSMA PET/CT scan?
items.a: A PSMA PET/CT scan is an imaging test that helps detect prostate cancer by targeting a protein called prostate-specific membrane antigen, which sits on the surface of most prostate cancer cells. A small amount of radioactive tracer binds to this protein and lights up on the scan, showing where cancer may be present. It is often used for staging or to check for recurrence, and its use should be guided by a qualified oncology team.

items.q: How does a PSMA PET/CT scan work?
items.a: A PSMA PET/CT scan works by injecting a radioactive tracer that attaches to PSMA proteins on prostate cancer cells. The PET part detects where the tracer collects, while the CT part provides detailed anatomical images, and the two are combined to pinpoint disease location. This helps show cancer that smaller or standard scans may miss. Interpretation depends on the individual case and should be reviewed by a nuclear medicine specialist and the treating team.

PSMA stands for prostate-specific membrane antigen, a protein found in high amounts on the surface of most prostate cancer cells. Because it is more common on cancer cells than on healthy tissue, it makes a useful target for imaging tracers and, in some cases, for targeted therapy. The level of PSMA can vary between patients and tumours, so scan findings should always be interpreted alongside other tests by a specialist team.

items.q: How is PSMA PET/CT different from a regular CT scan or bone scan?
items.a: PSMA PET/CT differs from standard CT or bone scans because it targets prostate cancer cells at a molecular level rather than only showing anatomy or bone changes. This often allows it to detect smaller deposits and spread earlier, including in lymph nodes or bone. It can be especially useful when PSA rises but conventional scans appear normal. Whether it adds value in a specific case depends on the clinical situation and specialist review.

items.q: Who is eligible for a PSMA PET/CT scan?
items.a: PSMA PET/CT may be considered for men with prostate cancer who need accurate staging, who have a rising PSA after treatment, or who are being assessed for PSMA-targeted therapy. It may be suitable for selected patients rather than everyone, and eligibility depends on cancer type, stage, PSA level, previous treatment, and overall health. A qualified oncology or nuclear medicine team should review the case and decide whether the scan is appropriate.

items.q: How do I prepare for a PSMA PET/CT scan?
items.a: Preparation for a PSMA PET/CT scan is usually simple, and your care team will give specific instructions based on the tracer used. In most cases you can eat normally, though you may be asked to stay well hydrated and empty your bladder before imaging. You should share details of your medications and recent treatments. Preparation steps can vary between centres and tracers, so always follow the exact guidance given by the imaging team.

items.q: Is a PSMA PET/CT scan safe?
items.a: PSMA PET/CT is generally considered safe and uses only a small amount of radioactive tracer, with radiation exposure broadly comparable to other nuclear imaging tests. Serious reactions are uncommon, and the tracer usually clears from the body within hours. As with any scan involving radiation, benefits and risks should be weighed for each person. Pregnancy or other health factors should be discussed with the imaging team before the scan.

items.q: What are the risks or side effects of a PSMA PET/CT scan?
items.a: Side effects from a PSMA PET/CT scan are usually minimal, and most patients experience little more than a brief pinch during the tracer injection. Rarely, some people may notice mild discomfort at the injection site or a temporary reaction. The scan does involve a small amount of radiation, which is why it is used only when clinically justified. Any concerns about side effects should be discussed with the nuclear medicine team beforehand.

items.q: How much does a PSMA PET/CT scan cost?
items.a: The cost of a PSMA PET/CT scan varies widely by country, hospital, and tracer used, so it cannot be quoted as a single fixed figure. Final cost also depends on the diagnosis, whether additional imaging is needed, the centre's pricing, and the treating team's advice. Some regions offer it at a lower cost than others. A personalised estimate should be obtained from the imaging centre after reviewing your medical details.

items.q: Is PSMA PET/CT available in India?
items.a: PSMA PET/CT is available at several major cancer hospitals and nuclear medicine centres in India, and the country is often chosen by international patients seeking advanced imaging at comparatively lower cost. Availability of specific tracers and appointment slots can vary between centres and cities. Because access, timing, and suitability differ by case, patients should confirm details directly with the hospital and have the scan recommended by a qualified oncology team.

items.q: Which countries offer PSMA PET/CT scans?
items.a: PSMA PET/CT is offered in many countries, including India, several European nations, Australia, parts of Asia such as China and Singapore, and, increasingly, the United States following regulatory approvals. Tracer types and availability differ by region and local approval status. Because access depends on centre capacity, tracer supply, and medical review, patients considering travel should confirm options in advance and rely on specialist guidance when choosing where to have the scan.

items.q: Is a PSMA PET/CT scan covered by insurance?
items.a: Insurance coverage for PSMA PET/CT varies by country, insurer, and the reason for the scan, so it cannot be assumed. Some policies cover it for staging or recurrence when clinically indicated, while others may classify it as non-standard or require pre-authorisation. Coverage rules also change as the scan becomes more widely approved. Patients should check directly with their insurer and treating team to confirm whether the scan is reimbursable in their situation.

items.q: Can PSMA PET/CT guide PSMA-targeted radioligand therapy?
items.a: PSMA PET/CT plays a key role in guiding PSMA-targeted radioligand therapy, such as Lutetium-177 PSMA treatment, by showing whether a patient's cancer expresses enough PSMA to respond. A scan that lights up strongly may indicate suitability, while low uptake may make the therapy less likely to help. This assessment is only one part of the decision, and final eligibility for radioligand therapy is determined by the treating oncology and nuclear medicine team.

items.q: Is PSMA PET/CT used in clinical trials?
items.a: PSMA PET/CT is frequently used in prostate cancer clinical trials, both to select patients and to measure how well new treatments work. Some trials use it to confirm PSMA expression before enrolling patients into targeted therapy studies. Taking part in a trial does not guarantee enrolment or benefit, as eligibility is decided after medical record review and investigator assessment against strict inclusion and exclusion criteria. Interested patients should discuss trial options with their specialist.

items.q: What tracers are used for PSMA PET/CT scans?
items.a: PSMA PET/CT scans use radioactive tracers that bind to the PSMA protein, with common examples including Gallium-68 PSMA and Fluorine-18 labelled PSMA agents. The choice of tracer depends on what a centre has available, local approvals, and technical factors, and each has its own imaging characteristics. Some newer tracers are still being studied. Which tracer is most appropriate for a given scan is decided by the nuclear medicine team performing the imaging.

items.q: What medical reports are needed before a PSMA PET/CT scan?
items.a: Before a PSMA PET/CT scan, centres usually ask for recent PSA results, prostate biopsy or pathology reports, prior imaging, and a summary of previous treatments such as surgery, radiation, or hormone therapy. These help the team confirm that the scan is appropriate and interpret the findings correctly. Exact requirements vary between hospitals and countries. International patients should confirm the needed documents in advance so the scan can be planned and reviewed accurately.

items.q: How can international patients access PSMA PET/CT scans abroad?
items.a: International patients can usually access PSMA PET/CT abroad by first sharing medical reports for review, then confirming scan availability, cost, and appointment timing with the chosen centre. Access also depends on hospital acceptance, visa approval, travel fitness, and the patient's overall condition, none of which can be guaranteed. Planning should include reports, cost estimates, travel, and follow-up care, with final decisions on imaging and treatment made by the treating oncology team.

items.q: How does CancerFax help patients with PSMA PET/CT?
items.a: CancerFax helps patients organize medical reports, identify relevant specialists or imaging centers, estimate possible costs, and coordinate second opinions, appointments, travel, visa, and follow-up support. Treatment decisions are always made by the qualified oncology team after reviewing the patient's diagnosis, stage, biomarkers, previous treatment, and overall health. CancerFax does not replace doctors or hospitals and cannot guarantee scan access, hospital admission, or specific outcomes.
